reader.decision: Approve the refresh-token delete in change_password, run in one transaction with the password update, relying on the 15-minute access expiry. Do not build the Redis marker now.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the SR-12 limit of 15 minutes equals ACCESS_TTL, so deleting refresh tokens meets it at one query per password change. The Redis marker adds a read to 2,500 requests per second and breaks the middleware rule in docs/architecture.md, and it is only needed if SR-12 demands faster revocation.

reconstruction.problem: change_password in api/auth/password.py updates password_hash and calls issue_tokens but never revokes the refresh tokens of the user's other devices. refresh_session does not check for a password change.
reconstruction.what_breaks: A stolen device keeps its 30-day refresh token. After the password change it can keep calling POST /auth/refresh every 15 minutes and stay logged in for up to 30 days.
reconstruction.fix: In change_password, add DELETE FROM refresh_tokens WHERE user_id = %s after the UPDATE users and before issue_tokens, in the same transaction as the update. refresh_session then finds no row and raises PermissionError. The thief is out within 15 minutes, and the laptop gets a fresh token pair. middleware.py and tokens.py stay unchanged.
reconstruction.cost: One query per password change and nothing per request. Remaining risks: an in-flight refresh_session on the stolen phone can insert a row after the delete (window of a few milliseconds, row lives 30 days), and the api.db transaction API was not found, so atomicity is unconfirmed.

follow_up_questions: Does SR-12 require revocation faster than 15 minutes, or is 15 minutes (ACCESS_TTL) acceptable?
What transaction API does api.db offer, so the UPDATE and DELETE run atomically?
Is the in-flight refresh race acceptable, or should refresh_session reject tokens issued before the last password change?
reader.closing_answer: Delete all of the user's refresh tokens in change_password, in one transaction, and rely on the 15-minute access expiry. No Redis marker for now. I would add it only if SR-12 turns out to require instant revocation. Please find the api.db transaction API and confirm the SR-12 wording.
